Online_WhatIs480Body: The OST kernel intercepts launch parameters and rewrites AppID to 480 (Spacewar), so Steam treats everyone as playing the same game for lobby matchmaking. Memory-only spoofing, no game files replaced.
Online_Step1: 1. In Steam library, right-click the game → Properties
Online_Step2: 2. Put the parameter below into Launch Options (advanced users)
Online_Step3: 3. Launch normally; remove the parameter to restore

Faq_Q1: Game download shows no internet connection
Faq_A1:
1. Check Settings → Kernel → upstream manifest source status, switch to a working source and retry (uninstall previously failed game cache first).
2. If all sources fail, use Manifest Monitor as fallback.
Faq_A2:
Denuvo games can't be played right after import. Extract tickets with an account that owns the game, then authorize with the ticket file — or find a crack patch.
Note: after Denuvo authorization, game/system/driver updates will invalidate it (bound to machine + game version).
Faq_A3:
A kernel conflict warning at startup means similar tools may have installed their kernels.
Use the toolbox (bottom-right) to purify common kernels; heavily modded ones must be removed manually.
If imported games still don't show, restart Steam; if that fails, the kernel isn't fully cleaned — consider reinstalling Steam.
Faq_Q4: Imported games missing from Steam library
Faq_A4:
1. Restart Steam after kernel install, or the hook won't take effect even if import reports success.
2. Imported games may briefly disappear after Steam launch: network issues can delay the upstream signature check, postponing the hook.
3. Multiple import kernels conflict — clean up old ones (see Kernel incompatible).
Faq_A5:
Cloud save errors are normal: manifest-imported games can't use official Steam Cloud.
Two options:
1. Just silence it: right-click game → Properties → disable cloud saves.
2. Use the in-app cloud save redirect (local or cloud drive) to fix it.
Faq_Q6: Cloud saves enabled but no effect
Faq_A6: Make sure the VC++ runtime is installed (hint at the top of the cloud page), then restart Steam (the DLL only reads config at startup).
Faq_A7: Wallpaper is classed as Software: in the Steam library filter at the top, tick Show software to display it.
Faq_Q8: Do imported games support online play?
Faq_A8:
Always-online games don't. For lobby/matchmaking games with friends, add -onlinefix to the game's launch options (both sides must do the same).
Or unlock online play with patches — see the in-app Online section.
Faq_A9: Yes, but the upstream manifest source must work (or use Manifest Monitor), plus a Workshop key. Then subscribing works.
Faq_Q10: Login stuck before extracting owned games
Faq_A10: Login uses official Steam endpoints, which can be slow from some regions. Enable a proxy/VPN and retry.
Faq_Q11: Online patch downloads slow or failing
Faq_A11: Patch sources are overseas — a proxy/VPN is required. Archive password is online-fix.me. Check the patch matches your game version.
Faq_A12: The key cache is a ~20MB JSON. If slow or stuck, switch networks or enable a proxy/VPN and restart the app.
Faq_A13: Turn off cover scraping in Display settings.
Faq_A14: Install the background service on the Trainer page and keep the binding's enable switch on.
Faq_A15: Fix it with Unpack in the app's No-Steam section.
Faq_A16:
First make sure Steam isn't on a Beta build. If it persists, follow method 2 in the error box: download a same-hash TOML from the method-3 upstream GitHub link, place it at the method-2 path, then restart Steam.
Or fetch it one-click from the bottom-right OST manager.
